title: A repeated ofal form marks a cross-register category rather than a local operation
summary: GDT811 records ofal/ofaldo at an f88r label, f88r prose occurrence, and f108r prose occurrence. Test whether this recurrence preserves a category or referent role across label/prose registers while local neighbours change, versus a productive operation whose role is supplied only by its local frame.

design.mechanism: The complete ofal form denotes a reusable category or referential class across label and prose registers, rather than a productive local operation.
design.unit: complete ofal/ofaldo occurrences with independently coded register, carrier relation, and local neighbour fields
design.contrast: cross-register category continuity versus frame-conditioned operation
design.prediction: After register and local neighbours are matched, category-role features should persist across the f88r label/prose and f108r prose occurrences; an operation model should predict a different role when the surrounding carrier or following field changes.
design.falsifier: On a predeclared held set with independent role coding, ofal/ofaldo follows local operation frames and shows no cross-register category continuity beyond exposure, falsifying this category model.
design.scope_note: The three occurrences do not independently identify a referent, species, suffix, or noun role. This is a source-starting exploratory question, not a claim that ofal is decoded.
design.related: Uses GDT811's narrower ofal lead; distinct from generic same-form reference tests because the unit is label/prose register transfer with explicit operation rival. Existing SEM card coverage and independent category binding must be checked before selection.
design.countermodel: A productive operation can recur at labels and prose positions because the same instructional template is reused, producing apparent cross-register continuity without category reference.

source_evidence.quote:
ofaldo/ofal is a narrower candidate for a learned name: one f88r label, one
f88r prose occurrence and one external prose occurrence at f108r.14. The
last source line is polchal shol qokar shedy pcholy qokal opchdy ofal shor
qokaiin otalod. No species, suffix or noun role is identified by that fact.

design.principal_risk: The register recurrence may be an exposure or template effect, and no independent referent/category annotation may exist.
